newsitem.title: EGYPT: Short Egyptian pound up against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Short Egyptian pound up against dollar.

text.p: The Egyptian pound rose against the dollar in the private-sector market on Monday after public-sector banks and firms had squared their positions ahead of the end of the financial year, bankers said.
"We've begun to see some offers of U.S. dollar and a shortage in the Egyptian pound," one banker said.

Another banker attributed the pound shortage to treasury bill auctions. The Central Bank has been auctioning for the past three weeks t-bills at a value exceeding the maturity by around 300 million pounds at each auction.
The latest offer is for 91-day bills worth 1.1 billion pounds at Wednesday's auction, replacing bills worth 665.3 million maturing on Thursday.
Private-sector bankers said the dollar ranged from 3.3955 to 3.3970 pounds bid and from 3.3965 to 3.3990 pounds offered in the interbank market.
A survey of four actively trading banks gave average rates of 3.3962 pounds bid and 3.3975 pounds offered. These averages compare to 3.3964 pounds bid and 3.3981 offered on Sunday.
The Central Bank calculated the average exchange rate at midday as 3.393554 buy and 3.398827 sell.
